Locating faults in this circuit may seem complex.
However, using the four step troubleshooting procedure that you learned in DC circuits makes finding faults easy.
The size and complexity of the circuit does not change the troubleshooting process.
Let's begin the lesson on ELECTRICAL CIRCUITS TROUBLESHOOTING...............
LESSON MENU
ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT FAULTS
The most common faults in an electrical circuit is an open or shorted component.
DISCUSSION
You have learned the circuit effects of opened or shorted resistors, capacitors, inductors, transformers and relays.
Basically, what is the effect of an opened component? an opened component?
An opened component is not eliminated from the circuit. Think about what happens to current through an opened resistor.
An opened component is not eliminated from the circuit. Think about what happens to current flow through an opened resistor.
An opened component is not eliminated from the circuit. Think about what happens to current flow through an opened resistor..
TRY AGAIN!
An opened component does not increase or decrease resistance, a changed value component does. However, you can say that an opened component does increase resistance to infinity!!!
TRY AGAIN!
INCORRECT2
"INCORRECT2"
Basically, what is the effect of a shorted component?
Eliminates the component from the circuit.
A shorted component does not prevent current flow, it allows maximum current flow.
A shorted component does not prevent current, it allows maximum current.
TRY AGAIN!
A shorted component does not increase or decrease resistance, a changed value component does. However, you can say that a shorted component does decrease resistance to zero!
TRY AGAIN!
The only component faults that you have not studied are the diode and LED.
If a diode or LED opens, current is prevented like any other opened component.
If a diode or LED opens, current flow is prevented like any other opened component.
The CRs will not allow a voltage to be developed at TP4. If one CR is open, the pulsating DC will be missing one cycle.
A shorted diode or LED acts as if the component was not in the circuit.
A shorted CR would allow current flow to TP4 in both directions. The AC would not be converted to pulsating DC.
A shorted CR would allow current to reach TP4 from both directions. The AC would not be converted to pulsating DC.
Finding the faulty component in this large circuit would be difficult if you did not follow a logical procedure.
The four step procedure that you have learned can be used.m
Find out if the circuit is operating correctly.
To determine if the circuit operates correctly, you measure the output voltages on TP10 and observe the LEDs.
With K1 de-energized, TP10 should measure an AC voltage and I2 should be illuminated..
With K1 energized, TP10 should measure a DC voltage and I1 should be illuminated.
Also, I3 intensity should change when the frequency of the input changes. The highest intensity is at resonance.
If these conditions are met, the circuit is operating correctly.
If not, then the circuit is faulted. Proceed to step 2.
Look for obvious faults in your circuit setup.
If the AC input voltage is not present, then there is no way that the circuit can operate correctly.
If your set up is correct and the circuit is still faulted, proceed to step 3.
Determine the possible fault or faults by making circuit measurements.
Use the schematic of the circuit and make measurements using test equipment.
Use all the information gathered as a guide to circuit measurements.
There is no need to measure signals from TP1 in circuit 1 to TP5 in circuit 2.
Check to see if K1 is faulted and if K1 is receiving the energizing voltage when circuit 2 S1 is depressed.

If the answer is yes, you have located the fault.
Repair the fault and repeat step 1. This ensures that the circuit has no other faults and is fully functional.
